title: Chapter 143 — The DOA: Dead on Arrival
intro: Brand new appliance, plugged in, does not work. The ultimate delivery nightmare.

sections.title: The DOA Protocol
sections.content:
Do not troubleshoot for 20 minutes while the customer watches you poke at their brand new $3,000 appliance. A DOA demands immediate ownership and immediate options.

Apologize without caveat. 'I am so sorry — this is completely unacceptable and I am going to fix it right now.' Then present options: Option A — expedited replacement. Pull from floor stock if needed. Same model, different serial number, delivered within 24-48 hours. Option B — full refund if they have lost confidence in the product. Option C — equivalent substitute from stock if the same model is not immediately available.

The speed of your response in the first 60 minutes determines whether this customer ever buys from you again. A DOA handled in 60 minutes is a story they tell positively. A DOA handled over 3 days is a Google review that haunts you.

sections.title: The Recovery
sections.content:
After the replacement is delivered and working: follow up the same day to confirm everything is running perfectly. Follow up again in 48 hours. Send a handwritten apology note — yes, handwritten. Consider a small gesture: a water filter, an accessory, a store gift card for their trouble.

A DOA handled with speed and grace can actually strengthen the relationship. The customer remembers how you responded more than they remember what went wrong. The Service Recovery Paradox is real — customers whose problems were resolved exceptionally become more loyal than those who never had a problem.

sections.title: Preventing Recurrence
sections.content:
After every DOA, report it to the manufacturer with the serial number. Track DOA rates by brand and model. If a specific model has a pattern, flag it to your purchasing team — it may need to be pulled or inspected at receiving.

Inspect high-value units at receiving when possible. A $5,000 built-in refrigerator is worth a 10-minute functionality check at the dock rather than discovering it is dead in the customer's kitchen with the cabinetmaker standing there.
